source.title: Class-wise Generalization Error: an Information-Theoretic Analysis
source.authors: Firas Laakom; Yu-Heng Bu; M. Gabbouj

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Empirically measures class-wise training–test generalization gaps and whether information-theoretic bounds track them, using a different measure and question from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports class-wise generalization errors and their relation to proposed CMI bounds. It does not test any listed version’s specific intervention or measure; its findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study measures class-specific training–test gaps and evaluates information-theoretic bounds. None of its experiments or theoretical arguments tests V1–V8. CMI tracking a gap does not test magnitude-aware sharpness in V7; 5% label noise does not test V1's random-label memorization comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that overfitting differs across classes, introduce class-specific MI and CMI bounds, and report empirical agreement between their bounds and class-specific gaps. Dependence on all ingredients of learning is their broader interpretation; the reported experiments do not isolate learning-algorithm effects.
record.recipe_differences: Measures class-wise generalization errors and information-theoretic bounds on CIFAR10 and noisy CIFAR10; it does not reproduce the listed versions’ experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and class change the observed class-wise error pattern; the trucks trend and the relative cat/trucks ordering differ between CIFAR10 and noisy CIFAR10.

fits_no_version.finding: Class-specific generalization gaps vary with class, sample count, and label noise. Section 3 reports that the trucks gap increases with sample count on noisy CIFAR10 and that the cat–truck gap ordering reverses between clean and noisy data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-specific training–test gaps can differ substantially and respond differently to sample count and label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that their class-∆y L-CMI bound scales approximately linearly with class-specific generalization gaps on clean and noisy CIFAR10; no correlation coefficient is supplied.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed class-dependent CMI bound tracks class-specific generalization gaps in the evaluated settings.

record.problems: Empirical CIFAR10 experiment uses m1 = 2 and m2 = 20; noisy CIFAR10 uses m1 = 5 and m2 = 15. Numerical class-wise errors and bound values are presented in figures rather than stated in the text. The reported correlation has no coefficient in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying outcomes were stated in text. Figures and appendix figures report further class-level results, but exact values are not recoverable from the supplied text.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label held-out accuracy and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Test-error trends when width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks, local connectivity, and initialization or learned sparsity conditions.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning and recovery recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes to training recipes.
Dropout effects, small-data and underfitting conditions, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness tracking generalization gaps and ranking them against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because every row links to none; this does not negate the descriptive findings. Generalization error here denotes a training–test gap, so a smaller gap alone does not establish higher held-out accuracy. No additional result bearing on a listed version appears in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; all named models and settings.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test-error trend.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer comparisons and tuning or recovery conditions.
Large versus small batch comparisons under epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparison against norm- and margin-based measures; the paper instead studies class-CMI bounds.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.
